ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Bella took a square piece of paper and folded two of its sides to lie along the diagonal, as shown, to obtain a quadrilateral. What is the largest size of an angle in that quadrilateral?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure shows a square, with a diagonal drawn from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner, and curved arrows indicating folding two sides toward this diagonal. The right figure shows the quadrilateral obtained after folding, in which the right side and bottom side still maintain the directions of the original square's sides. Reasoning: According to the method, label the square as A being the upper-left corner, B being the upper-right corner, C being the lower-right corner, D being the lower-left corner, and the diagonal is AC. The diagonal AC of the square makes 45° with both sides AB and AD. When folding, the crease is the angle bisector of the angle between the original side position and the position after folding that lies on diagonal AC, so the angle between each crease and the corresponding original side is half of 45°, namely 22.5°. In the quadrilateral after folding, the lower-right corner is still the original square angle, 90°. The two angles formed where the creases intersect the original right side and bottom side are respectively 90° + 22.5° = 112.5°. The other small angle is 45°. Therefore the largest angle in the quadrilateral is 112.5°.

raw_record.question_text: Bella took a square piece of paper and folded two of its sides to lie along the diagonal, as shown, to obtain a quadrilateral. What is the largest size of an angle in that quadrilateral?

method.method_draft: Label the square in the left panel as A top-left, B top-right, C bottom-right, D bottom-left, with the drawn diagonal AC. From the image, the curved arrows show that the top side AB and left side AD are folded inward so that they lie along diagonal AC; the right panel shows the resulting quadrilateral whose other two sides remain portions of the original right and bottom sides. Use the folding fact that a crease is the angle bisector between the original position of a folded side and its final position. Since AC is a diagonal of a square, it makes 45° with both AB and AD. Therefore each crease makes half of 45°, i.e. 22.5°, with the corresponding original side. In the final quadrilateral, the bottom-right angle is the original square corner, 90°. The two angles where the creases meet the original bottom and right sides are each 90°+22.5°=112.5°, while the angle at A between the two creases is 45°. Hence the largest angle is 112.5°.

method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer gives 112.5°, which matches the standard answer exactly.
